transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2027-11-10 14:00 PST | Duration: ~52 minutes
Attendees: Maya (Redwood CSM), Ethan (Redwood Onboarding Eng), Jules (Redwood SE), Dr. Alicia, Tom, Sana, Marco, Priya (Riverside)

Summary: quick kickoff to align on pilot goals, security, infra, and next steps.

00:00 - 00:38 Maya: Hey everyone, thanks for joining — this is Maya Singh, I'm the CSM for Riverside, with Ethan and Jules from our onboarding and SE teams. Quick round robin?
00:40 - 01:05 Dr. Alicia: Hi all, Alicia here. Head of data at Riverside. We're excited to get this moving — we want a pilot by end of month.
01:06 - 01:30 Tom: Tom Reyes, engineering manager. I'll be the main infra contact.
01:32 - 01:55 Sana: Sana Patel, security. I'll own compliance & KMS questions.
02:00 - 02:22 Maya: Great, thanks. Objectives for today: confirm scope, security constraints, and timeline for staging keys and SE deep-dive.
02:25 - 03:10 Jules: I'll high-level the runtime and deployment options — we support hosted (API), Dedicated reserved pools, and Private (VPC/on-prem). For pilot most customers start hosted for speed, then Dedicated or Private for stricter isolation.
03:15 - 04:00 Tom: Quick question — how does VPC connectivity work? We have strict egress rules and private subnets.
04:05 - 05:00 Ethan: Right so for Private we can either do VPC peering / PrivateLink or ship an on-prem package. For hosted we need an IP allowlist and TLS, but PII concerns usually push customers to Dedicated or Private.
05:10 - 06:00 Sana: We are SOC2 in scope, and we use customer-managed KMS for secrets. Can you integrate with our KMS/HSM? Also retention — we can't retain PII beyond 30 days for some datasets.
06:05 - 07:00 Jules: We support KMS integrations (AWS KMS/GCP KMS and HSM via KMIP for Private). For hosted we offer envelope encryption and can work with KMS for key wrapping; we'll follow up with the security whitepaper.
07:10 - 08:00 Marco: On the product side, main success criteria: latency for inference under 200ms p95 for our short prompts, and cost per 1000 queries to be reasonable. Pilot should show latency and quality metrics.
08:05 - 09:00 Ethan: For latency, traffic pattern matters. We can recommend batching and KV/prefix caching to keep costs down and latencies low. We'll propose a config tailored to your qps.
09:05 - 10:00 Tom: For the staging environment, we need test API keys and a way to route to a sandbox model. What's the provisioning timeline?
10:05 - 11:00 Maya: Redwood can provision staging keys within 2 business days once we have the account info and IP allowlist. We'll also share a quickstart repo.
11:10 - 12:00 Sana: About SSO — we use SAML with Okta, we'd need SSO for the console and RBAC for teammate roles.
12:05 - 13:00 Jules: We support SAML/SSO and SCIM for provisioning. We'll share SSO setup doc; CSG can walk through configuration in the next call.
13:10 - 14:00 Dr. Alicia: A note on data residency — some patients are in EU, do you have region guarantees?
14:05 - 15:00 Maya: Hosted has region selection; Private allows you to keep inference in your VPC/region. For strict residency we recommend Private or Dedicated with region pinning.
15:05 - 16:00 Marco: What's the plan for model variants? We want ability to fallback if capacity or quality issues.
16:05 - 17:00 Ethan: We support automatic fallback routing policies and model pinning. For pilot we'll propose a single model variant with a fallback to a compatible quantized variant if needed.
17:10 - 18:00 Tom: Network ports and egress — do you need specific CIDR ranges?
18:05 - 19:00 Maya: Yes we'll provide IP ranges for allowlist and advise on firewall rules. We'll ask for PRD of your network and we can produce a checklist.
19:10 - 20:00 Sana: Audit logs and retention — we need full request/response audit logs for a 12 month retention window for certain endpoints. Is that available?
20:05 - 21:00 Jules: We surface audit logs in the console and can stream logs to your SIEM. Retention tiers are configurable; we'll share options (and premium retention is an add-on).
21:10 - 22:00 Dr. Alicia: For pilot data, we'll use de-identified records, but eventually need PII throughput. How strict is Redwood on redaction?
22:05 - 23:00 Ethan: We advise client-side redaction and tokenization for PII, and server-side we have masking and retention controls. We'll include best practices in the onboarding docs.
23:10 - 24:00 Marco: Timeline check — we want a two-week pilot: week 1 integration + week 2 evaluation. Is that realistic?
24:05 - 25:00 Maya: Yes that's a common cadence. We'll target staging keys by 2027-11-13, SE deep-dive week of 2027-11-16, and pilot run 2027-11-20 to 2027-11-27.
25:10 - 26:00 Tom: Can we do a small benchmark run for throughput? We'll send a synthetic workload.
26:05 - 27:00 Jules: Perfect — we'll run a latency/throughput benchmark and share latency p50/p95 and cost estimates.
27:10 - 28:00 Sana: Who at Redwood is our security contact?
28:05 - 29:00 Maya: I'll introduce you to our security lead in an email thread after this call and attach the security pack (SOC2 report, pen test summary, network checklist).
29:10 - 30:00 Dr. Alicia: Ok great. Any blockers from Redwood side for staging?
30:05 - 31:00 Ethan: Just account provisioning and IP allowlist. Also want a test dataset and example prompts to tune config.
31:10 - 32:00 Tom: We'll share the infra diagram and example prompts by 2027-11-15.
32:05 - 33:00 Maya: Action items recap — I'll send onboarding deck + SSO guide by Friday.
33:10 - 34:00 Marco: Do you offer cost optimization suggestions for embedding-heavy workloads?
34:05 - 35:00 Jules: Yes, caching/quantization and hybrid models can help. We'll include recommended quant profiles for your expected payload sizes.
35:10 - 36:00 Sana: Encryption in transit + at rest ok? We need TLS 1.2+, and KMS only keys for secrets.
36:05 - 37:00 Jules: Confirmed, TLS and KMS supported; we'll surface details in security doc.
37:10 - 38:00 Maya: Next steps and who owns what — quick run-through.
38:05 - 39:00 Maya: Maya: Send onboarding deck & SSO doc (due 2027-11-12).
39:05 - 40:00 Tom: Tom: Share infra diagram & IP allowlist (due 2027-11-15).
40:05 - 41:00 Ethan: Ethan: Prepare pilot config & benchmark plan (due 2027-11-16).
41:05 - 42:00 Sana: Sana: Confirm KMS/HSM requirements and return security checklist (due 2027-11-17).
42:10 - 43:00 Dr. Alicia: Great — shall we schedule the SE deep-dive now?
43:05 - 44:00 Maya: We'll send a poll for week of 2027-11-16; prefer mornings PST.
44:10 - 45:00 Marco: Anything else?
45:05 - 46:00 Maya: One last note: we'll provide dashboards for latency/cost per route; expect an initial cost estimate after the benchmark.
46:10 - 47:00 Jules: Also note fallback policies and canary rollouts are supported if you want gradual production ramp.
47:05 - 48:00 Tom: Sounds good. Thanks, everyone.
48:10 - 49:00 Maya: Thanks all — we'll follow up with the docs and invites.
49:10 - 52:00 (crosstalk / wrap up) short clarifications, laughter, off-mic logistics.

Action items (in transcript):
- Maya: send onboarding deck, SSO doc, security pack

- Tom: infra diagrams and allowlist
- Sana: confirm KMS details
